To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) demand management is a viable approach to managing environmental water requirements; (2) demand management can be used to manage water for the environment in a way that is consistent with existing water rights and responsibilities; (3) demand management can provide a more equitable framework for water allocation, and (4) a better understanding of the environmental water requirements is needed before demand management can be effectively applied.
